description: Maya is holding the family's inherited grandfather clock and must make the final decision about who receives it, where it will stand, how it will be moved and serviced, and when it may chime, with input from four relatives.

shared_context.S1: The family has inherited one working grandfather clock from their late grandfather, and Maya is currently keeping it in her hallway.
shared_context.S2: The family wants the clock placed in a relative's home rather than sold or discarded.
shared_context.S3: Maya will make the final decision about the clock's recipient, placement, move, servicing, and chime settings.
shared_context.S4: The clock is currently wound and has been running normally in Maya's hallway.
shared_context.S5: As a family habit before settling an heirloom decision, Maya goes around the room and asks each person for anything that should shape the plan.

PF1.text: Nora found a signed estate note among the grandfather's papers stating that the clock is to go to Rosa, the youngest grandchild; she has not shown the note to the group yet.

PF2.text: Rosa's townhouse stairwell is 78 centimeters wide while the clock case is 82 centimeters wide, so the clock cannot reach an upstairs room there and must stand in Rosa's ground-floor dining room; Rosa told Eli this when discussing the move.

PF3.text: A horologist who inspected the clock told Ben that it should be transported upright by a specialist piano-and-clock mover and serviced before it is wound again; this recommendation has not reached the family.

PF4.text: Sofia's infant sleeps beside Rosa's dining room, and Rosa asked her to make sure the clock's chimes are silenced from 20:00 through 07:00; Sofia has not raised this with Maya.

acceptance_conditions: The clock must be assigned to Rosa in accordance with the estate note.
The clock must be placed in Rosa's ground-floor dining room because it cannot pass through her 78-centimeter stairwell.
The clock must be transported upright by a specialist piano-and-clock mover.
A commitment must require servicing the clock before it is wound again.
The chimes must be silenced from 20:00 through 07:00.
The settlement must cite Nora's estate-note fact after she states it aloud.

decisive_facts.why: The signed estate note changes the recipient from an open family choice to Rosa specifically and supplies the fact that must be cited.
The 78-centimeter stairwell versus the clock's 82-centimeter case changes the placement from an upstairs option to Rosa's ground-floor dining room.
The horologist's recommendation changes transport to an upright specialist move and adds the exact service-before-winding commitment.
The infant's sleeping schedule changes the clock's chime setting to silence from exactly 20:00 through 07:00.
